cards.stem: What baseline amount of emergency savings does the rule describe?
options: three months’ worth of living expenses
six to nine months’ worth of living expenses
a federally insured bank or credit union
cards.quote: save 10 percent of what you earn, and have at least three months’ worth of living expenses saved up in case of an emergency
cards.hint: Recall the minimum emergency cushion described.

cards.stem: Which larger savings buffer is mentioned as better if possible?
options: six to nine months’ worth of living expenses
three months’ worth of living expenses
cards.quote: Explain that, if possible, it’s better to have more savings—like six to nine months’ worth of living expenses, instead of only three.
cards.hint: Consider the bigger cushion noted as better when possible.

cards.stem: Where is money suggested to be kept for safety?
options: a federally insured bank or credit union
a retirement account at work called a 401(k)
cards.quote: Talk about how to keep money in a safe place, like a federally insured bank or credit union.
cards.hint: Remember the safe insured place mentioned.
